1.title: Managing and Deploying Resources
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Managing and Deploying Resources. It covers the exam area Describe Azure management and governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Describe the Azure portal. Describe Azure Cloud Shell, Azure C L I, and Azure Power Shell. Describe the purpose of Azure Arc. Describe infrastructure as code. Describe Azure Resource Manager (A R M) and A R M (Azure Resource Manager) templates. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure management and governance (thirty to thirty-five percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Ways to manage Azure
1.text: Ways to manage Azure. All of these tools send the same requests to Azure Resource Manager, so you can use whichever fits the job. Azure portal. Style: Web graphical interface. Best for: Learning, exploring, one-off tasks, dashboards. Azure Cloud Shell. Style: Browser-based command line (Bash or Power Shell). Best for: Quick commands from any device, no install. Azure C L I. Style: Cross-platform command-line tool ( A Z ). Best for: Scripts and automation, many platforms.

1.title: Ways to manage Azure, continued
1.text: Ways to manage Azure. Azure Power Shell. Style: Power Shell cmdlets (Az module). Best for: Automation for people who use Power Shell. A R M templates or Bicep. Style: Declarative files (infrastructure as code). Best for: Repeatable, consistent deployments. R E S T (representational state transfer) A P Is and S D Ks. Style: Code. Best for: Custom applications.

1.title: Ways to manage Azure, continued
1.text: Ways to manage Azure. The figure shows this: Portal, Cloud Shell, C L I, Power Shell and templates all call Azure Resource Manager.

1.title: The Azure portal
1.text: The Azure portal. The Azure portal is a web-based graphical console for building, managing and monitoring Azure resources. Works in a browser, no installation, usually with point-and-click steps. Offers customizable dashboards, search and a view of all resources. Great for learning and occasional tasks; not ideal for repeating the same work many times (manual steps are slow and can differ each time).

1.title: Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell
1.text: Cloud Shell, Azure C L I and Azure Power Shell. What. Azure Cloud Shell: Browser-based shell hosted by Azure. Azure C L I: Cross-platform command-line tool. Azure Power Shell: Module of cmdlets for Power Shell. Install? Azure Cloud Shell: No (opens from the portal). Azure C L I: Yes (Windows, mac O S, Linux). Azure Power Shell: Yes (Windows, mac O S, Linux). Language. Azure Cloud Shell: Bash or Power Shell. Azure C L I: Commands start with A Z. Azure Power Shell: Cmdlets named like Get Az V M.

1.title: Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell, continued
1.text: Cloud Shell, Azure C L I and Azure Power Shell. Typical use. Azure Cloud Shell: Run quick commands anywhere. Azure C L I: Scripts and automation. Azure Power Shell: Scripts and automation.

1.title: Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell, continued
1.text: Cloud Shell, Azure C L I and Azure Power Shell. Cloud Shell comes with Azure C L I and Azure Power Shell already installed and is authenticated with your account. It keeps files in an Azure Files share (a storage account is used for persistence). C L I and Power Shell can do the same tasks; the choice is about preference, not capability. Both support scripts, so they make work repeatable and automatable. Exam tip: No installation, in the browser to Cloud Shell. A Z commands to Azure C L I. Get Az... cmdlets to Azure Power Shell. Graphical to portal.

1.title: Azure Arc
1.text: Azure Arc. Azure Arc extends Azure management and services to resources outside Azure: on-premises, in other clouds and at the edge. With Arc you can. Project servers, Kubernetes clusters and databases into Azure as Arc-enabled resources. Apply Azure Policy, tags, R B A C, monitoring and Defender for Cloud to them like Azure resources. Run some Azure services (such as Azure data services) anywhere. Exam tip: "Manage on-premises or other-cloud servers from Azure with a single control plane" to Azure Arc. It supports hybrid and multicloud management.

1.title: Infrastructure as code (IaC)
1.text: Infrastructure as code. Infrastructure as code means defining your infrastructure in files and deploying it by running them, instead of clicking in a portal. Consistency. The same file gives the same result every time. Repeatability. Create test, staging and production the same way. Speed and automation. Deploy a whole environment in minutes. Version control. Store the files in source control, review and roll back. Documentation. The file itself describes the environment. Two styles: declarative (you describe the end state: "I want these resources", and the platform works out how) and imperative (you list the steps). A R M templates and Bicep are declarative; scripts with C L I or Power Shell are usually imperative.

1.title: Azure Resource Manager and ARM templates
1.text: Azure Resource Manager and A R M templates. Azure Resource Manager (A R M) is the deployment and management service for Azure. Every request from the portal, C L I, Power Shell, S D Ks or templates goes through A R M, which authenticates, authorizes and then performs the action. A R M lets you. Manage resources as a group (resource groups) and apply access control, tags, locks and policy. Deploy many resources together in the right order with dependencies. Get a consistent experience across all tools. A R M templates are Jason files that declare the resources to deploy.

1.title: Azure Resource Manager and ARM templates, continued
1.text: Azure Resource Manager and A R M templates. Declarative. Describe what you want, not the steps. Idempotent. Deploying the same template again gives the same result, with no duplicates. Repeatable and reusable. Use parameters to change names, sizes or regions. Orchestration. A R M deploys resources in parallel or in order based on dependencies. Modular. Split big deployments into linked or nested templates. Bicep is a simpler language that compiles to A R M templates. Exam tip: "Deploy the same environment repeatedly and consistently" to A R M template. "Every request goes through one management layer" to A R M. Jason plus declarative plus idempotent to A R M template.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors needs to deploy identical test and production environments again and again with no manual differences. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A R M templates (infrastructure as code). Templates are declarative, repeatable and consistent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An administrator wants to run Azure commands from a browser on any computer without installing software. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Cloud Shell. Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell with C L I and Power Shell ready.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants to manage its on-premises Windows and Linux servers with Azure Policy and Defender for Cloud. Which service enables this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Arc. Azure Arc projects non-Azure resources into Azure so Azure management tools apply.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which service receives every management request, whether it comes from the portal, C L I or a template? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Resource Manager. A R M is the single management layer for Azure resources.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which statement about A R M templates is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: They are declarative Jason files and can be deployed repeatedly with the same result. A R M templates declare the desired state and are idempotent.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which commands belong to Azure C L I? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Commands starting with A Z. Azure C L I commands start with A Z. Get Az V M is an Azure Power Shell cmdlet.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which tool is a web graphical interface? Answer: The Azure portal. Question two. Which two shells are available in Cloud Shell? Answer: Bash and Power Shell. Question three. What does Azure Arc do? Answer: Extends Azure management to on-premises, other clouds and the edge.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is infrastructure as code? Answer: Defining infrastructure in files that are deployed automatically, for consistent and repeatable results. Question five. What does idempotent mean for a template? Answer: Deploying it again gives the same result with no duplicates. Question six. What is Bicep? Answer: A simpler language that compiles to A R M templates.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Portal: web gooey; learn and one-off tasks. Cloud Shell: browser shell, Bash or Power Shell, no install, C L I and Power Shell included. C L I versus Power Shell: A Z commands versus Get Az... cmdlets; both cross-platform and scriptable. Azure Arc: manage on-premises, multicloud and edge resources from Azure. I A C: infrastructure in files: consistent, repeatable, fast, versioned; declarative versus imperative. A R M: the management layer all tools use; groups, access control, locks, policy. A R M templates: declarative Jason, idempotent, parameters, dependencies; Bicep compiles to them. In the next module, we continue the course.
